description: An iPhone battery, charging and thermal instrument built on private iOS APIs — real charger watts, what actually reaches the cell, all 30 temperature sensors, and the USB-PD handshake.

latest_release.name: v1.7.0
latest_release.body:
Unsigned build — sign it with your own Apple ID before installing.
https://github.com/ResistanceTo/MiniWatts#install

## 改进

- **温度可以显示为华氏度。** 设置 → 单位 里可选"自动 / °C / °F"。"自动"跟随系统地区，以及"设置 › 通用 › 语言与地区"里的"温度"选项，所以地区使用华氏度的用户升级后会直接看到 °F。App 各页、图表、热力图、悬浮读数、实时活动和小组件都按所选单位显示；原始数据仍显示传感器给出的 °C。(#25)
- **充电预估。** 充电时，功率页会显示充到 80% 和充到 100% 还要多久，以及大约几点。时间根据电量实际上升的速度推算，不依赖电池能量设置；要等电量变化两次才会出现，通常需要几分钟。80% 以后按典型充电曲线估算，只是近似值。(#27)
- **显示版本号。** 设置 → 关于 里显示当前版本，原始数据导出的第一行也带上了版本号。(#27)
- **iPad 布局。** iPad 横屏和 13 英寸竖屏时，各页分成两栏；窄屏时仍是一栏。历史记录里单次充电的详情页在 iPad 上不再横向铺满。(#22)
- **iPad 热力图。** 在 iPad 上，发热页画的是 iPad 的轮廓，各区域按 iPad Pro 11 英寸的内部布局放置：主板在中间，两侧是电芯，充电芯片在 USB-C 接口旁。设备页和设置里的图标也换成了 iPad。(#13, #22)

## 修复

- 发热：CPU 簇（`pACC`、`eACC`）和图像处理器（`ISP`）等传感器以前被归入"其他传感器"，现在算作 SoC，SoC 区域的温度也会把它们算进去。iPhone 11 上 `FrontCameraDie`、`BCMLBSkin` 这类名字连写的传感器以前会被分错区（比如前摄像头被当成机身），现在会先拆词再归类。(#13, #14)
- 适配器页里"单次采样"那段说明以前在中文界面下一直显示英文，现在已有中文。

## 注意

- iPad 相关的改动只在模拟器里验证过，我手上没有 iPad。如果在 iPad 上看到问题，请从 设置 → 原始数据 复制导出并反馈。
- iPad 上"来自充电器"的功率偏低（#13）这次还没有修：要确认其余的输入由哪个传感器测量，需要一份**充电时**导出的原始数据。有 iPad 的话，请在充电时从 设置 → 原始数据 复制导出，贴到 #13。
- 充电预估无法知道是否开启了充电上限或优化电池充电。如果开着，电池会在上限前停下，"充到 100%"的时间就不准。

---

## Improvements

- **Temperatures can be shown in Fahrenheit.** Settings → Units offers Automatic, °C or °F. Automatic follows your region and the Temperature option under Settings › General › Language & Region, so if your region uses Fahrenheit you will see °F straight after updating. Every page, the charts, the heat map, the floating meter, the Live Activity and the widget follow the setting; Raw data still shows the sensors' own °C. (#25)
- **Charge forecast.** While charging, the Power page shows how long until 80% and until 100%, and roughly when. It is worked out from how fast the battery level is actually rising, so it does not depend on the battery energy setting; it appears once the level has moved twice, usually within a few minutes. Past 80% it follows a typical charging curve and is approximate. (#27)
- **Version number.** Settings → About shows the installed version, and the first line of the Raw data dump includes it. (#27)
- **iPad layout.** On an iPad in landscape, and a 13-inch in portrait, every page uses two columns; narrower windows keep one. A session's detail page in History no longer stretches edge to edge on an iPad. (#22)
- **iPad heat map.** On an iPad the Thermal page draws an iPad, with the zones placed as in an iPad Pro 11-inch: logic board down the middle, a battery cell either side, the charge IC by the USB-C port. The Devices page and Settings use iPad icons too. (#13, #22)

## Fixes

- Thermal: the CPU-cluster (`pACC`, `eACC`) and image-processor (`ISP`) sensors used to land under "Other sensors"; they now count as the SoC, and the SoC zone's temperature includes them. On an iPhone 11, run-together sensor names such as `FrontCameraDie` and `BCMLBSkin` were filed in the wrong zone (the front camera as chassis); names are now split into words before they are matched. (#13, #14)
- Adapter: the one-sample note always showed in English in the Chinese interface; it is now translated.

## Notes

- The iPad changes were checked in the simulator only — I do not have an iPad. If something looks wrong on yours, copy the dump from Settings → Raw data and report it.
- The low "from charger" reading on an iPad (#13) is not fixed yet: finding which sensor carries the rest of the input needs a Raw data dump taken **while charging**. If you have an iPad, please copy one from Settings → Raw data while it charges and post it on #13.
- The charge forecast cannot tell whether a charge limit or Optimized Battery Charging is on. If one is, the battery stops short and the time to 100% will be wrong.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ResistanceTo/MiniWatts/compare/v1.6.0...v1.7.0

detail.readme: # MiniWatts **English** · [简体中文](README.zh-Hans.md) [![Build](https://github.com/ResistanceTo/MiniWatts/actions/workflows/build.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/ResistanceTo/MiniWatts/actions/workflows/build.yml) An iPhone and iPad battery and charging monitor built on Apple's private APIs. It reads the device's own power-management sensors — the ones iOS uses to run the charge — and shows what the charger is delivering, how much of it reaches the cell, where the rest goes as heat, and what every temperature sensor in the device is doing while it happens. | Power | Thermal | Adapter | History | |:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:| | | | | | > **Sideload only.** Private APIs mean this can never be on the App Store — you sign > and install it yourself. There is no network code of any kind: nothing it reads > leaves your phone. ## Install Download the latest `MiniWatts-unsigned.ipa` from [Releases](https://github.com/ResistanceTo/MiniWatts/releases) and sign it with your own Apple ID — [Sideloadly](https://sideloadly.io), [AltStore](https://altstore.io), [SideStore](https://sidestore.io) and Xcode all do this. A free Apple ID works; the app then expires after seven days and you re-sign it. Requires iPhone or iPad, iOS 17 or later. Or add the source to SideStore or AltStore — including the SideStore bundled with LiveContainer — and install from there, so new versions show up as updates: ``` https://github.com/ResistanceTo/MiniWatts/releases/latest/download/apps.json ``` LiveContainer cannot run app extensions, so installed inside it MiniWatts has no widget and no Live Activity. MiniWatts includes a Home Screen and Lock Screen widget, and a Live Activity while charging. The widget extension is one more App ID when you sign — a free Apple ID gets ten a week — and if your signing tool offers to remove extensions, doing so removes the widget. ## What it can't do Sensor names, scales and even which sensors exist differ by device model, and none of it is documented. This build was written and verified on an iPhone Air; on another model a reading can be missing or mean something other than its name suggests. Impossible values — a charge IC at −9199 °C, which someone really did see — stay in Raw data for diagnosis but are left out of derived temperatures; a wrong value that looks plausible cannot be caught that way. Please report anything surprising with your model identifier. Only what iOS actually hands a sandboxed app. Battery health and cycle count are filtered out of the registry; accessory batteries (Watch, AirPods) come back empty; wireless charging exposes no input current, so on MagSafe you only see what reaches the cell; discharge power has no sensor and is estimated from the percentage. Charging holds can only be inferred, and the app labels them `inferred` when that is what happened. For wired charging, the live input number is measured at the phone's USB-C rail (`VQ0u × IQ0u`). The adapter's advertised watts are a negotiated ceiling, while a wall meter includes the adapter and cable losses, so those figures describe different points in the power path and should not be expected to match. Widgets refresh when iOS decides to, usually every 15 to 60 minutes, and each one shows when its numbers were taken. The Live Activity only updates while MiniWatts is running; once the app is suspended it shows the reading as paused. Neither can be made to update once a second — that budget is the system's to spend, not the app's. For a reading that does move once a second while you are in another app, open the floating meter from Settings: a small Picture in Picture window that keeps MiniWatts running, so it also records the charge with the screen locked. It costs battery, and you close it yourself. It plays no sound — Picture in Picture is a video feature, which is the only reason the app declares audio playback at all. ## Build Xcode 26 or later, iOS 17 deployment target, no dependencies. ```bash ./scripts/build-ipa.sh # unsigned, what Releases ships TEAM_ID=ABCDE12345 ./scripts/build-ipa.sh signed # signed, for your own device ``` [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md) is the engineering notebook: which APIs the sandbox blocks and how that was established, what each sensor turned out to be, and the Swift 6 isolation traps this project has already fallen into. ## Licence Apache 2.0 — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). The method for reading the PMU is derived from [ios-charging-monitor](https://github.com/gregsramblings/ios-charging-monitor) (MIT); `BatteryCenterBridge` owes two details to [Batsie](https://github.com/leptos-null/Batsie). Both are credited in [NOTICE](NOTICE), which carries the upstream MIT notice. Private APIs can change or disappear in any iOS update.
